🔹 In every government,…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Ghabl_enghelab

📝 "On the occasion of Paknejad's farewell"

🔹 In every government, there's always a fight over who gets the top spots — in SHASTA, in the holdings, in the pension funds, in the petrochemical companies, and elsewhere — when it comes to managing the wealthy ministries.

🔹 No matter how you slice it, the relevant minister's team, the President's office team, the First Vice President's team, teams tied to security institutions, and so on — each marches to its own beat, trying to install its own people and take out the rival's.

Personally, I don't think Mr. Pezeshkian has enough charisma or leadership strength to manage these conflicts within the government.

But none of these fights and power struggles are new.

🔹 The country's new problem in recent years is the Islamic Consultative Assembly.

As a supervisory body that shouldn't be meddling in the government's internal fights, it now has a speaker who's clearly unhappy with where he is and wants to install his left and right hands, his affiliates and associates, everywhere from the Privatization Organization to the pension fund to the Persian Gulf Holding to a thousand other places — and he himself has become a party to all these fights.

🔹 Just a few days ago, in the middle of the war between the trusts and their mutual exposés, in the middle of the infighting within the government, I heard that Mr. Ghorbanzadeh — a member of the negotiating team and Mr. Ghalibaf's right-hand man — was removed from the board of directors of the Persian Gulf Holding. I guessed right then that the Oil Minister's departure was certain.

🔹 I say this as a friend: in this situation, the Assembly has lost its supervisory function, and a new party has been added to the government's internal fights, draining its energy.

#Vahid_Ashtari

🔴@ghabl_enghelab
